title: Automated escalation attachments that extract KV/trace snippets for faster on-call triage
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: On-call responders waste time opening multiple consoles to assemble context: top spans, slowest KV cache hits, recent model rollouts, and correlated errors. Goal: push a compact, prioritized attachment bundle into PagerDuty incidents and Slack alert threads that contains 1) a ranked trace snippet (top 3 spans by latency + their parent/child context), 2) a summarized KV/cache hitmap for the request path, 3) recent deploy/rollout info and compatible fallback model variant, and 4) a draft postmortem skeleton with suggested timeline and owners. Scope: prototype server-side extractor and enrichment webhook for PagerDuty/Slack, UI flag in Console to toggle attachments per escalation policy, and a small eval harness to ensure attachments are < 50KB and remove PII. Success criteria: mean time to first meaningful action (MTFMA) for oncall reduced by 30% in pilot team; attachments delivered within 500ms of initial alert; attachment size < 50KB 99% of the time; no new failure modes introduced in the alerting pipeline.
updates: 2026-02-25: Proposal and spike completed. Implemented a PoC that can extract top spans from 1k-trace sample and generate a 3-span summary. Added a KV-hit sampler that produces a histogram of key prefixes.

2026-03-03: Design review with SRE and Security. Key feedback: redact all user identifiers and paginate attachments when size exceeds threshold. Security asked for KMS-backed signing of attachment bundles so PD/Slack can verify authenticity.

2026-03-07: Prototype endpoint /v1/ops/enrich created (internal-only). Integration test sends a PagerDuty webhook to our enrichment service which replies with 'attachments' payload. Observed 320ms median processing time for 95th percentile traces sampled at 1:10. Identified expensive op: span retracing across multiple trace storages when trace is sharded.

2026-03-10: Trade-off decision: to meet 500ms SLO we'll prefer local cache read + incomplete but prioritized trace snippet instead of full trace rehydration. This reduces fidelity but speeds delivery. Documented fallback policy in design doc.

2026-03-12: Working on adding Console toggle and RBAC control for which escalation policies can include sensitive attachments. Draft PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/784 (WIP).
comments: PM review - Jonah Patel: Love the MTFMA metric. Please include a user-facing opt-out and an audit log entry for attachment reveals.
SRE - Mei Chen: Need to ensure enrichment service scales horizontally and has no single-host chokepoint. Suggest using async fan-out to PD/Slack once enrichment bundle is signed.
Security - Tomasz Nowak: Confirmed redaction checklist. Also require a feature flag gating signing until KMS integration completes.
Design - Priya Desai: Suggest visual compacting rules for Slack attachments (use code blocks + collapsible summaries) to prevent noise during noisy incidents.
